clue.text: Move about hospital in an expeditious way abroad

indicators.note: the hospital letter is set inside the shuffled letters
to move these words is to shift their letters around into a new order

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Someone advises shifting a patient round the hospital in a hurried, foreign fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to the German motorway: 'abroad' tells you the road is foreign.
explanation.definitionFit: A German motorway is built for fast travel, so it is a speedy road found in another country.

clue.text: A group of musicians in accompaniment

parts.note: LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra

explanation.surface: A band of players performs in accompaniment.
explanation.walkthrough: The LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: Also means as well or in addition, along with something else.

clue.text: Bite from insect coming up

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a gnat is a small flying insect

explanation.surface: A bite from an insect that is rising into the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' reverses GNAT in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A tang is a sharp, biting flavour.

clue.text: Union member properly in prison once

parts.note: a bride is one partner in the union of marriage
to do something well is to do it properly

explanation.surface: A trade unionist behaving properly while in jail long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' suggests a trade union; it is marriage. Bridewell was a London prison, and the name came to mean any jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridewell, after the London house of correction, was a historical word for a prison.

clue.text: Bear assailant undercover

parts.note: a bear hug is a crushing embrace, so a bear is one who hugs
a mugger attacks people in the street

explanation.surface: A bear and a street attacker are working secretly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' suggests the animal or to endure; read it as one who gives bear hugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugger-mugger means secret or clandestine, as well as muddled.

clue.text: Smoke tobacco primarily in retirement, like King Lear

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the letters are read in the backward direction

parts.note: a cigar is something you smoke

indicators.note: primarily points to the opening letter of tobacco

explanation.surface: An old king who has given up power puffs on his cigar in retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retirement' turns the whole of CIGAR plus T backwards, giving TRAGIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's King Lear is one of his great tragedies, so its hero is a figure of tragedy.

clue.text: Foreign money available without capital holds up

indicators.note: holds means the shortened word contains the next piece
without its capital means losing the first letter

parts.note: something free is available

explanation.surface: Overseas funds are not to be had without capital, which holds things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds up' reads as a phrase meaning delays, but 'holds' is the container signal and 'up' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupee is the currency of India, Pakistan and other countries.

clue.text: Torment in sea capsizing in strong wind a good deal here?

indicators.note: the second in sets the built-up piece inside the wind word

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind

indicators.note: the first in puts the torment word inside the upturned sea
a capsizing boat turns over, so the word is upended and read backwards

parts.note: to rag someone is to tease or torment them

explanation.surface: Sailors are tormented as their ship capsizes in a gale.
explanation.walkthrough: The inner build is ARAGES, which sits between the G and the ALE of the wind word; the question mark marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: At a garage sale household goods go cheap, so a buyer may find a bargain there.

clue.text: Withdrawal from distant country

parts.note: a cold person is aloof or distant
Turkey is a country

explanation.surface: Pulling out of a faraway nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold turkey is abrupt withdrawal from an addictive drug.

clue.text: Capital, generous character cut short by villainous one

indicators.note: cutting short means losing the final letter

parts.note: Santa Claus is the figure famous for handing out gifts
Iago is the scheming villain of Shakespeare's Othello

explanation.surface: A kindly figure is cut down by a wicked rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' removes the last A of SANTA, leaving SANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Santiago is the capital city of Chile.

clue.text: Chaos of Paris at end of mortal coil

indicators.note: chaos means disorder, so the letters of the city name are jumbled
at the end of points to the final letter of mortal

explanation.surface: A Hamlet-like line about the disorder in the French capital at the close of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chaos of' rearranges PARIS into SPIRA; 'mortal coil' is from Hamlet's soliloquy, and the definition is just 'coil'.
explanation.definitionFit: A coil winds round and round, which is the shape of a spiral.

clue.text: Nazi work encompassed by terror most wicked

indicators.note: encompassed by means the work piece sits inside the jumbled letters
wicked suggests letters behaving badly, out of their right order

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A deed surrounded by the most wicked terror.
explanation.walkthrough: Both the definition and the fodder are dark in tone, so the surface hides the join well.
explanation.definitionFit: Storm troopers were members of the Nazi paramilitary force, the SA.

clue.text: Old disc opening into eye, visible?

annotationWithheld.why: Old disc opening into eye, visible? : VENT ('opening') goes into EYE, and that goes in SIGHT; 'visible' must give both SIGHT and the container signal (in sight), one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Old disc opening into eye, visible?

clue.text: Nazi boy almost captured by queen perhaps, where she's most powerful

indicators.note: captured by means the pieces are held inside the card word

parts.note: a queen is an example of a playing card
Rudolf Hess was a leading Nazi

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A young Nazi is caught by a queen, on the board where she rules.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads straight across the whole surface: 'captured' and 'queen' play on the game too.
explanation.definitionFit: The queen is the strongest piece in chess, so the board is where she has most power.

clue.text: Cynical, not prepared for soldiers?

definitions.meaning: tough and unsentimental, especially of a writer or detective
soldiers are strips of toast dipped into a runny egg, which a firmly cooked egg will not suit

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'soldiers' are fingers of toast dipped into a soft-boiled egg.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough, unsentimental character is called this, and an egg cooked solid cannot take toast soldiers.

clue.text: Call to Maria perhaps to follow man in drag

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
Ave, as in Ave Maria, is a greeting or call to the Virgin Mary

explanation.surface: A hymn-like call to Maria comes after a man dressed in women's clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drag' looks like cross-dressing; it is the verb to pull hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave something is to haul or pull it with great effort, which is to drag it.

clue.text: Duck in second half of cricket season: good wickets lost in reply

indicators.note: taking only the second half means the first three letters go

parts.note: cricket is played in the summer

indicators.note: lost means the wickets letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: an answer is a reply
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wickets

explanation.surface: A cricket report: late in the summer the side lost wickets in their reply innings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second half of' keeps MER from SUMMER; 'lost' takes W out of ANSWER, leaving ANSER. A 'duck' in cricket is a score of nought, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The merganser is a fish-eating diving duck with a serrated bill.

clue.text: Planner distraught about house that's blown up

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around the house abbreviation
distraught means upset, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A planner is in despair about a house that has been blown up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blown up' tempts as exploded, fitting the distraught planner; it means played by blowing.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpenhorn is a long wooden horn played by blowing, so it is blown into.

clue.text: Car part is to be returned, please

indicators.note: returning something sends it back, so the short word is read backwards

parts.note: to please someone is to delight them

explanation.surface: A request to return a faulty component from a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be returned' reverses IS to SI.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidelight is a small lamp at the front or side of a vehicle.

clue.text: Bean often sought medically?

definitions.meaning: edible seeds of the pea family, such as beans or lentils
a doctor commonly feels for the heartbeat at the wrist

explanation.definitionFit: Beans and lentils are pulses, and the throb of the blood a doctor checks is also called by this word.

clue.text: Detail on cake gains nominal mark

indicators.note: in an across clue, a piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: a brownie is a small chocolate cake
a point is a detail or particular

explanation.surface: Fancy icing on a cake earns a token reward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detail on cake' looks like icing; it is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A brownie point is an imaginary credit for good behaviour, a mark that exists in name only.

clue.text: With no head for thought, mother is childlike

indicators.note: with no means the letter is taken away

parts.note: a mother tongue is a native tongue, so mother means native

indicators.note: the head for a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A mother who has no head for thinking behaves like a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head for thought' is T; 'With no' takes it out of NATIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive means innocent and unworldly, as a child is.

clue.text: Dog's breakfast or dinner in canteen

definitions.meaning: British slang for a muddle or shambles
a meal eaten together in a military dining hall

explanation.definitionFit: A muddle is a mess, and the armed forces call their communal meal and dining room the mess.

clue.text: Shock seeing Times leader in unlikely location?

indicators.note: in means the letter sits inside the newspaper name

parts.note: The Sun is a rival British tabloid, an odd place to find the Times

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Shock as the Times's editorial turns up in an unlikely paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' looks like the editorial; it is the first letter, T. The Sun is a British tabloid, a rival of the Times.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun someone is to shock or stagger them.

clue.text: White said to indicate approval in Spain, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the entry sounds like the word given

parts.note: ole is the Spanish cry of approval at a bullfight or dance

explanation.surface: A white coffee is said to win Spanish approval, so people report.
explanation.walkthrough: French AU LAIT is said 'oh-lay', like Spanish OLE; 'said' is a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee served with milk is called white coffee in Britain, the French phrase meaning with milk.

clue.text: Eton falsely admitting pressure doubled on rival

indicators.note: admitting means letting something in, so the shuffled letters contain the new piece
falsely means the letters are set out in a wrong order
doubled means the letter appears twice

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure

explanation.surface: A rival school is accused of falsely letting in double pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffle makes OONENT, and the doubled letter goes in after its first O.
explanation.definitionFit: An opponent is someone on the other side of a contest, a rival.

clue.text: Duke given more rum to go falteringly

parts.note: rum means odd or strange, so more rum is odder

explanation.surface: A duke given extra rum staggers along unsteadily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' tempts as the drink; here it is the old British adjective for strange.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodder is to move shakily and unsteadily, typically from age.

clue.text: George etc, missing an old relative .

parts.note: GR is the royal cipher of King George, Georgius Rex

indicators.note: missing means a letter is left out

parts.note: etc. stands for and so on
O is the abbreviation for old, and an means just one of them

explanation.surface: A list of Georges and others that lacks one elderly family member.
explanation.walkthrough: GR plus AND SO ON gives GRANDSOON; 'missing' drops one O.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandson is the son of one's child, a family relative.
